results.content: *Store features in Vertex AI Feature Store and schedule Dataflow to compute transformations, then deploy the scikit-learn model with the prebuilt prediction container to Vertex AI Endpoints and use Vertex AI batch prediction for offline scoring* is unnecessary for this scenario because Feature Store manages feature storage and serving rather than performing per request inference time normalization. *Add a pipeline component that pushes metrics to Vertex AI Model Registry, then monitor metrics with Cloud Monitoring dashboards* misuses the services because the Model Registry is for model versions and related artifacts rather than per run training metrics, and Cloud Monitoring focuses on operational telemetry rather than custom experiment metrics. #### Cameron’s Google Cloud Certification Exam Tip. When a question asks for the easiest collaboration across runs with both programmatic access and interactive visuals, think of *Vertex AI Experiments* with *ML Metadata* for tracking and *Managed TensorBoard* for visualization rather than building custom storage and dashboards.

results.content: # A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality — Part 1 — Data Quality, Defined: Fitness‑for‑Use, Not Perfection. This guide shows how to achieve fitness-for-use through data contracts, lineage, observability, and a practical operating model — eschewing unattainable perfection for measurable business value. > **Series note.** This article is part of **A Pragmatic CDO’s Field Guide to Data Quality** — a 10‑part, artifact‑driven playbook for making data fit‑for‑use across BI/analytics, ML, and GenAI. **Series at a glance:** (1) Data quality, defined; (2) where it breaks; (3) metrics, data contracts, observability, identity/MDM; (4) stewardship, SCD/CDC, reconciliation, backfills; (5) AI that helps (not hypes); (6) retail playbook; (7) finance playbook; (8) healthcare playbook; (9) tools that scale (OSS, enterprise, hyperscalers); (10) the CDO’s 12‑month operating playbook;. Dr. Adnan Masood is an Engineer, Thought Leader, Author, AI/ML PhD, Stanford Scholar, Harvard Alum, Microsoft Regional Director, and STEM Robotics Coach.
